title: Coca-Cola Q3 2026 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenue Rises 7% and Guidance Raised
excerpt: Comparable EPS rose 11% to $0.91 on net revenues of $13.4 billion as global volume grew 5%, led by India, China, Mexico and Brazil; Coca-Cola lifted its 2026 EPS and free cash flow outlook.
body:
• Coca-Cola's third-quarter comparable earnings rose 11% year over year to $0.91 per share, beating consensus estimates of $0.87 to $0.88, while net revenues grew 7% to $13.4 billion, ahead of the $12.93 billion estimate.
  • Global unit case volume grew 5%, led by India, China, Mexico and Brazil; Coca-Cola Zero Sugar volume rose 16% and Trademark Coca-Cola grew 5%, while North America volume was flat.
  • Operating income grew 12% and operating margin expanded to 33.4% from 32.0%; reported earnings rose 8% to $0.93 per share, with net income of about $4.0 billion.
  • Coca-Cola raised its full-year 2026 outlook: comparable EPS growth of at least 11%, organic revenue growth of at least 5%, and free cash flow of at least $13 billion, up from about $12.4 billion.

The Coca-Cola Company beat earnings and revenue estimates for the third quarter on Tuesday and raised its full-year outlook, as broad-based volume growth across emerging markets — led by India, China, Mexico and Brazil — more than offset a flat quarter in North America. It was a beat built on selling more drinks, not just charging more for them.

Net revenues grew 7% to $13.4 billion in the quarter ended in September, and organic revenues also grew 7%, driven by a 7% increase in concentrate sales and 1% growth in price/mix, according to the company's third-quarter release. Comparable earnings per share rose 11% to $0.91, beating the $0.87 Zacks consensus, while reported EPS grew 8% to $0.93. Zacks put reported revenue at $13.35 billion against a $12.93 billion consensus estimate.

"Our results this quarter demonstrate our system's sustained momentum, giving us confidence in our updated full year guidance. By staying close to consumers and executing with agility across our global system, we are delivering quality growth."

— Henrique Braun, Coca-Cola CEO

Volume Growth, Led From Abroad

Global unit case volume grew 5% for the second consecutive quarter. Sparkling soft drinks grew 5%, with Trademark Coca-Cola up 5% and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar up 16% across all geographic segments, while Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Light grew 6%. Juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverages were even, as growth in fairlife, Maaza and Minute Maid offset the sale of finished product operations in Nigeria. Water, sports, coffee and tea grew 5%, led by an 8% rise in water, while sports drinks declined 3%.

Geography told the story. Latin America volume grew 6%, with organic revenue up 16% on pricing and mix, helped by momentum in Mexico and Brazil. Asia Pacific volume also grew 6%, with India's top brands delivering double-digit growth, and Europe, Middle East and Africa volume grew 5%. North America was the outlier: unit case volume was flat as Trademark Coca-Cola growth was offset by declines in water, sports, coffee and tea, and organic revenue growth eased to 3%. Management pointed to holiday shipment timing and softer restaurant traffic, with at-home consumption outperforming away-from-home channels.

Margins and Cash Flow

Operating income grew 12%, and operating margin expanded to 33.4% from 32.0% a year earlier; comparable operating margin was 32.9%, versus 31.9%. Comparable currency neutral operating income grew 8%, as organic growth and currency tailwinds outweighed higher marketing investment and operating expenses. Both reported and comparable EPS included a 2-point currency tailwind. Coca-Cola also gained value share in total nonalcoholic ready-to-drink beverages. Year to date, cash flow from operations was $12.5 billion and free cash flow was $11.4 billion.

Guidance Raised

The beat came with a raise. For full-year 2026, Coca-Cola now expects organic revenue growth of at least 5%, comparable EPS growth of at least 11% — up from 9% to 10% — including an approximate 3% currency tailwind, and comparable currency neutral EPS growth excluding acquisitions and divestitures of at least 9%. Free cash flow guidance rose to at least $13.0 billion, from about $12.4 billion, on at least $15.2 billion of operating cash flow and about $2.2 billion of capital spending. The underlying effective tax rate is now seen at 19.7%. With volumes growing across most of the world, the raised outlook rests on demand holding up in emerging markets while North America steadies.
